                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The primary way of working with Entities in Wasp is with Queries and Actions, collectively known as **.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'In the Wasp Spec,\n'[39m +

                      [32m'### Queries and actions​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Wasp DSL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Wasp Spec\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getTasks {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We do that by defining Operations, in this case, a Query `getRecipes` and Action `addRecipe`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'which are in their essence Node.js functions that execute on the server and can, thanks to Wasp, very easily be called from the client.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'First, we define these Operations in our `main.wasp.ts` file, so Wasp knows about them and can "beef them up":\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getRecipes, addRecipe } from "./src/recipe/operations" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Function: query()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/api/@wasp.sh/spec/functions/query)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> **query**(`fn`, `config?`): `Query`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a Query definition.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries are server-side read-only operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'They can be invoked from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the client (with caching via `useQuery`) and the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'List the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities the query reads from so Wasp can inject the matching Prisma\n'[39m +
                      [32m'delegates into `context.entities` and invalidate the client cache when\n'[39m +
                      [32m'related actions modify them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### fn ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Reference`<`AnyFunction`>\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Reference to the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### config?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### auth?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`boolean`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Whether this Query requires auth.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If your app has auth enabled, this\n'[39m +
                      [32m'defaults to `true`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Only available if your app has auth enabled.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### entities?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`string`[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A list of entities you wish to use inside your Query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'See Using Entities in Queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTasks } from './src/queries' with { type: 'ref' }\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query(getTasks, { entities: ["Foo"] }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Queries - Wasp - ContextQMD\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.12/data-model/operations/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the Query in Wasp using the `query` declaration.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Define the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Using Entities in Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In most cases, resources used in Queries will be Entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To use an Entity in your Query, add it to the `query` declaration in Wasp:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getAllTasks {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { getAllTasks } from "@src/queries.js",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Task]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getFilteredTasks {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { getFilteredTasks } from "@src/queries.js",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Task]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Declaring Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `query` declaration supports the following fields:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `fn: ExtImport` <Required />\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The import statement of the Query's NodeJs implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- `entities: [Entity]`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A list of entities you wish to use inside your Query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For instructions on using Entities in Queries, take a look at the guide.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getFoo {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { getFoo } from "@src/queries.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Foo]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The command\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Migration from 0.15.X to 0.16.X - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-07, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.19/migration-guides/migrate-from-0-15-to-0-16)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To migrate your Wasp app from 0.15.X to 0.16.X, follow these steps:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Bump the Wasp version ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Update the version field in your Wasp file to `^0.16.0`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'app MyApp {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'version: "^0.16.0"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Update the package.json file ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Make sure to explicitly add `react-dom` and `react-router-dom` to your `package.json` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dependencies": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"react-dom": "^18.2.0",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"react-router-dom": "^6.26.2"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Update the tsconfig.json file ​\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Seeding a Database with Prisma (TypeScript) - Robin Wieruch\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-03-21, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://www.robinwieruch.de/prisma-seeding-database/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We will create a new TypeScript file called **seed.ts** in the **prisma** folder.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';\n"[39m +

                      [32m"{ name: 'Post 3' },\n"[39m +

                      [32m'const seed = async () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// clean up before the seeding (optional)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await prisma.post.deleteMany();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// you could also use createMany\n'[39m +

                      [32m'await prisma.post.create({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'});\n'[39m +

                      [32m'create: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"providerName: 'email',\n"[39m +

                      [32m"providerData: sanitizeAndSerializeProviderData<'email'>({\n"[39m +
                      [32m'password: data.password,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'isEmailVerified: true, // Set isEmailVerified to true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this example,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'sanitizeAndSerializeProviderData\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you seed a database with Prisma? - Benevolent Bytes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-08-03, last updated: 2026-07-07, [Read more](https://blog.sethcorker.com/question/how-do-you-seed-a-database-with-prisma/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The key things to in your seed script are:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Import the Prisma client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Create the records you want to seed in your DB using the client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Await the creation of these records (otherwise node will terminate too soon)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To tell Prisma that we have a seed, we need to add a property to our package.json:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"prisma": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"seed": "ts-node prisma/seed.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.11.8/tutorial/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The primary way of interacting with entities in Wasp is by using queries and actions, collectively known as *operations*.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To call a Query on the client, you can import it from `wasp/client/operations` and call it directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- Make sure you pass in a `context` object with the `user` field to authenticated Queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Declaring a Query enables you to import and use it anywhere in your code (on the server or the client).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, for a Query that we declared as `getFoo`, Wasp generates two functions with the same name that you can import and use:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Queries - Wasp - ContextQMD\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.12/data-model/operations/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To use a Query, you can import it from `wasp/client/operations` and call it directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When using Queries on the client, you can make them reactive with the `useQuery` hook.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This hook comes bundled with Wasp and is a thin wrapper around the `useQuery` hook from *react-query*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The only difference is that you don't need to supply the key - Wasp handles this for you automatically.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's `useQuery` hook is a thin wrapper around the `useQuery` hook from *react-query*.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's `useQuery` hook accepts three arguments:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- `queryFn` <Required />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The client-side query function generated by Wasp based on a `query` declaration in your `.wasp` file.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `queryFnArgs`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The arguments object (payload) you wish to pass into the Query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The Query's NodeJS implementation will receive this object as its first positional argument.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- `options`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *react-query* `options` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use this to change\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the default behavior for this particular Query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to change the global defaults, you can do so in the client setup function.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Function: query() | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/functions/query)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> **query**(`fn`, `config?`): `Query`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a Query definition.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries are server-side read-only operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'They can be invoked from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the client (with caching via `useQuery`) and the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'List the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities the query reads from so Wasp can inject the matching Prisma\n'[39m +
                      [32m'delegates into `context.entities` and invalidate the client cache when\n'[39m +
                      [32m'related actions modify them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Reference`<`AnyFunction`>\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Reference to the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use reference imports when passing values from your app into the Wasp spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If a direct import is not practical, use ref as a fallback.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Example ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTasks } from './src/queries' with { type: 'ref' }\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query(getTasks, { entities: ["Foo"] }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# Wasp\n'[39m +

                      [32m'1import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" };\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# React Query questions - Wasp\n'[39m +

                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- In Wasp, the cache keys are handled internally and are not expected to be supplied by the user.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is done by the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object, which you can use to change the default behavior for this particular Query (**source**(https://wasp-lang.dev/docs/data-model/operations/queries#the-usequery-hook-1)).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to access the Query cache key, you can do so by accessing the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Here is an example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Wasp uses React Query under the hood for data fetching and caching, and it provides a thin wrapper around the'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# QueryClient | TanStack Query Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-03, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/v4/docs/reference/QueryClient)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The QueryClient can be used to interact with a cache:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const queryClient = new QueryClient({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'defaultOptions: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queries: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'staleTime: Infinity,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m"await queryClient.prefetchQuery({ queryKey: ['posts'], queryFn: fetchPosts })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- queryCache?: QueryCache - Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The query cache this client is connected to.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- mutationCache?: MutationCache - Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The mutation cache this client is connected to.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- logger?: Logger - Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The logger this client uses to log debugging information, warnings and errors.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If not set, console is the default logger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'prefetchQuery is an asynchronous method that can be used to prefetch a query before it is needed or rendered with useQuery and friends.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The getQueryCache method returns the query cache this client is connected to.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Quick Start | TanStack Query React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/quick-start)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This code snippet very briefly illustrates the 3 core concepts of React Query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Mutations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Query Invalidation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useQuery,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useMutation,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useQueryClient,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'QueryClient,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'QueryClientProvider,\n'[39m +
                      [32m"} from '@tanstack/react-query'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTodos, postTodo } from '../my-api'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Create a client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const queryClient = new QueryClient()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function App() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Provide the client to your App\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<Todos />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'</QueryClientProvider>\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function Todos() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Access the client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const queryClient = useQueryClient()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Mutations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const mutation = useMutation({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'mutationFn: postTodo,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'onSuccess: () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate and refetch\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<ul>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{query.data?.map((todo) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'))}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Query Invalidation | TanStack Query React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-05, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-invalidation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For that purpose, the QueryClient has an invalidateQueries method that lets you intelligently mark queries as stale and potentially refetch them too!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate every query in the cache\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryClient.invalidateQueries()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate every query with a key that starts with `todos`\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a query is invalidated with invalidateQueries, two things happen:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- It is marked as stale.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This stale state overrides any staleTime configurations being used in useQuery or related hooks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- If the query is currently being rendered via useQuery or related hooks, it will also be refetched in the background\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Get QueryClient from the context\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const queryClient = useQueryClient()\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryKey: ['todos'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you find yourself wanting **even more** granularity, you can pass a predicate function to the invalidateQueries method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function will receive each Query instance from the query cache and allow you to return true or false for whether you want to invalidate that query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'predicate: (query) =>'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# React TanStack Query: Server State and Caching Guide (2026)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://techoral.com/react/tanstack-query.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install @tanstack/react-query @tanstack/react-query-devtools\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Query keys identify and cache your queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Treat them like dependency arrays:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Static key — same data for all users\n'[39m +
                      [32m"useQuery({ queryKey: ['settings'], queryFn: fetchSettings })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Dynamic key — separate cache entry per userId\n'[39m +
                      [32m"useQuery({ queryKey: ['user', userId], queryFn: () => fetchUser(userId) })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Nested objects — filter params\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useQuery({\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryKey: ['products', { category, page, sort }],\n"[39m +
                      [32m'queryFn: () => fetchProducts({ category, page, sort }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate all product queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['products'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['products', { category: 'shoes' }] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Key convention:** Use arrays with a resource name first, then identifiers, then filters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This lets you invalidate at different levels of specificity.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate — marks stale, refetches if observed\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['posts'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['posts'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m')'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# React Query의 setQueryData 활용한 캐싱된 데이터 업데이트 훅 소개\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-11-03, last updated: 2025-09-30, [Read more](https://algoroot.tistory.com/171)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'**useSetQuery.ts 훅 소개**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'주어진 조건에 따라 원하는 쿼리 키를 검색할 수 있습니다.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const updateQueryData = ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 단일 쿼리 데이터 업데이트\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const updateInfinityQueryData = ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 무한 리스트 쿼리 데이터 업데이트\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const rollback = ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 이전 데이터로 롤백\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  const { data: tasks, isLoading: tasksLoading, error: tasksError } = useQuery(getTasks)\n'[39m +

                  [32m'      await addTask({ title, projectId })\n'[39m +

                  [32m"      alert('Failed to add task: ' + err.message)\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2024-03-18, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1219368012918948003)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migrate-dev Ensures dev database corresponds to the current state of schema(entities):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Generates a new migration if there are changes in the schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Applies any pending migrations to the database either using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'supplied migration name or asking for one.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'OPTIONS:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'--name [migration-name]\n'[39m +

                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev --name "Added User entity"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# CLI Reference | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-05-27, last updated: 2025-11-24, [Read more](https://wasp-docs-on-main.pages.dev/docs/0.18.0/general/cli)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`wasp db migrate-dev`synchronizes the development database with the current state of the schema (entities).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If there are any changes in the schema, it generates a new migration and applies any pending migrations to the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`--name foo`option allows you to specify a name for the migration, while the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`--create-only`option lets you create an empty migration without applying it.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/deployment/database)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Migrations are some code that describes the change you made in the schema, and they are used to apply the change to the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'After you made a change in the Prisma schema, you can create a migration by running the following command:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This command will create a new migration in the `migrations` directory.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/databases)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL=<production-db-url> wasp db seed myProductionSeed\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To run your Wasp app in production, you'll need to switch from SQLite to PostgreSQL.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'1. Set the provider to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"postgresql"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'provider = "postgresql"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'url = env("DATABASE_URL")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'rm -r migrations/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp clean\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Ensure your new database is running (check the section on connecting to a database to see how).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Leave it running, since we need it for the next step.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. In a different terminal, run\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A Gentle Introduction to Database Migrations in Prisma ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-02, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/blog/2025/04/02/an-introduction-to-database-migrations)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Once you've written a Prisma schema for your app, you'll need to create a **migration file.** This file will contain SQL commands needed to update your database, such as creating new tables or modifying existing ones, or adding database indexes, etc.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Let's run `wasp db migrate-dev` which uses the Prisma CLI in the background and you'll get the following code in the `migrations/` dir:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `wasp db migrate-dev` gives us this migration file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Warnings:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Made the column `score` on table `Match` required.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This step will fail if there are existing NULL values in that column.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-- AlterTable\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ALTER TABLE "Match" ALTER COLUMN "score" SET NOT NULL;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Always do database changes through migrations (they keep local and production databases in sync)'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp db migrate-dev questions - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-22, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1298345230881525852)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command in Wasp is used to synchronize your development database with the current state of your schema, which is defined by your entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If there are any changes in the schema, it generates a new migration and applies any pending migrations to the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This command primarily executes Prisma commands behind the scenes [^1^].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It does not migrate your local database to your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. Instead, it ensures that your development database corresponds to the current state of your schema. If you have made changes to your entities, you would need to run\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to create a new migration reflecting these changes and apply it to your database [^5^].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to connect to an existing database, you can set the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'environment variable in your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.env.server\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file or inline when running the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# start-dev-server\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-24, last updated: 2026-06-05, [Read more](https://www.claudepluginhub.com/skills/wasp-lang-wasp-plugins-wasp/start-dev-server)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If this is the first time starting the app, or if there are pending migrations, run the following command:\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Directory Verification:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use listFiles to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - cd "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - cd /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail)\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Capture the output of the command.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- The command argument is required.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- You can specify an optional timeout in seconds (up to 300s). If not specified, commands will timeout after 60s.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple executeCommand tool calls in a single message. For example, if you need to run "git status" and "git diff", send a single message with two executeCommand tool calls in parallel.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'  - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)\n'[39m +
            [32m"- You shall avoid use the markdown code block syntax (backtick, '`') in your command, as it will be interpreted as a command substitution.\n"[39m +
            [32m"- Before using this tool, you must first think about the context provided in <system-reminder> to understand the user's environment and tailor your commands to ensure they are compatible with their system. You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Create the commit with a message ending with:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'Commit message here.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'EOF\n'[39m +
            [32m')"\n'[39m +
            [32m'</example>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Use the description/body for details, not the title\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands in parallel:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Create new branch if needed\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting.\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'## Summary\n'[39m +
            [32m'<1-3 bullet points>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## Test plan\n'[39m +
            [32m'[Checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]\n'[39m +

            [32m'🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +
            [32m'EOF\n'[39m +
            [32m')"\n'[39m +
            [32m'</example>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Return the PR URL w'[39m... 332 more characters,
